subject: computer-science
title: Memory Hierarchy and Cache
welcome_lead: From registers to disk: navigate the memory pyramid for blazing performance.
meta_desc: IBDP CS adventure on memory hierarchy, cache levels and locality of reference.
final_note: Faster memory is smaller and pricier - hence the hierarchy!

concepts.def: Layers from fastest registers to slow disk.
Small fast memory between CPU and RAM.
Cache levels increasing in size and latency.
Volatile main memory for running programs.
Recently used data likely used again soon.
Requested data found in cache; fast access.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Top: registers (ns access, KB). Middle: L1/L2/L3 caches.

Then RAM (ns-μs, GB), SSD/HDD (ms, TB).

Temporal: same item again soon (loops).

Spatial: nearby items soon (arrays). Cache exploits both.
